steps.title: Write down who it's for and the one thing they should take away
Draft the script as 6-8 bullet beats with a hook in the first line
Sketch a rough shot list, one line per beat
Add timing and camera notes to each shot in your list
Read the script aloud once and trim any lines that feel slow
Set up your filming spot and record one 10-second test clip
Record just the hook line until you have one clean take
Film the remaining shots on your list in one sitting
Assemble a rough cut: lay the clips in order, no polish yet
Watch the rough cut once and write down 2-3 fixes (cuts, pacing, audio level)
Make those fixes and add captions or a title card
Export as vertical 1080x1920 and watch it once on your phone
Create the channel (or update name, handle and a 3-line bio)
Write the title, a 3-sentence description and 3-5 tags for this video
Upload the exported video, pick a thumbnail frame and hit publish
Open your video's analytics and write down just two numbers: views and average view duration
Jot 2 things that worked and 1 thing you'd change next time, one line each
Pick your video-two idea and write its one-sentence promise
Write a concept card: working title, one target viewer, and the one takeaway they should remember
Write three different opening hooks (first 5 seconds) and pick the strongest one
Draft the full 45-60 second script, one line per beat (hook, setup, payoff, call to action)
Turn the finished script into an 8-10 shot list: for each shot note framing (wide/close), what happens, and its seconds on screen
Read the script aloud against the shot list with a stopwatch and trim any line so the whole thing lands under 60 seconds
Do a 60-second camera test: record one shot in your actual filming spot and check light, sound, and framing on playback
Film every shot on your list in one session: two takes per shot, and re-shoot any take where the framing or sound fails your camera-test standard
Assemble a rough cut: lay all clips on the timeline in script order and trim each to its planned seconds until the cut runs under 60
Polish pass on the rough cut: add captions, level the audio, fix one thing that bugs you, and export the final file
Create the channel on your chosen platform: name, handle, profile image, and a one-line bio that matches your concept card's promise
Write the upload package: a title under 60 characters, a 2-sentence description with your takeaway as the first line, 3 tags, and the exact cover/thumbnail text
Upload the final file as a private/unlisted draft with the full upload package, then watch it start to finish on your phone and write down every fix needed before it goes public

Work down the fix list from your private-draft watch-through: fix the top three items, re-export, and flip the video to public — then note the exact publish time and paste the link somewhere you'll see it

Pull the first numbers on the published video (views, average view duration, likes/comments) and mark on the retention graph the exact second where most viewers drop off — one screenshot, one sentence on why

Turn that drop-off second plus the best-performing moment into a one-page brief for video two: the lesson you're applying, a working title, the target viewer, and the single takeaway — no shot list yet
Turn your one-page video-two brief into a written promise, a target viewer, and three candidate hooks — then pick the hook that directly fixes the retention-drop second
Draft video two's 45–60 second script in one sitting, opening with the chosen retention-fix hook and reusing the beat structure that worked in video one
Convert video two's script into an 8-shot list with seconds per shot, and label the first shot as the retention-fix shot — stop before filming
Learn the open G and C chords and check each string rings cleanly
Practice slow switches between Em, Am, C and G for 10 minutes
Strum steady downstrokes on one chord while counting 1-2-3-4 out loud
Practice a down-up strumming pattern (D-DU-UDU) on a muted strum for 10 minutes
Do a 10-minute metronome drill switching between Em, Am, C and G at a slow tempo
Pick one easy 2-3 chord song and play its chord changes with steady downstrokes
Play your chosen song's chord progression with the D-DU-UDU pattern at a slow tempo for 15 minutes
Learn the chord shapes and changes for a second easy 2-3 chord song
Play both songs back-to-back once each without stopping to build stamina
Play your first song start to finish once and note the shakiest chord change
Loop that shakiest chord change slowly for 10 minutes until it feels smooth
Play the same song again with a soft verse and a louder chorus to practice dynamics
Record yourself playing your first song once on your phone, then listen back and write down two things to fix
Spend 15 minutes fixing those two spots slowly with a metronome, then play the song once more
Do a full run-through of the song standing up, playing it start to finish without stopping, as a dress rehearsal
Set your phone up to record and capture one full standing take of your song from start to finish
Listen back to the recording and loop the one spot that slips for 10 minutes with the metronome
Play the song live once for a friend or family member, or record and share a second full take
Learn the D chord and check each string rings cleanly
Learn the G chord and do 5 minutes of slow Em–Am–D–G changes with a metronome at 40 bpm
First strumming rep: steady all-downstroke 4/4 pattern over Em–Am–D–G, 5 clean laps in a row
Learn the C chord, check each string rings, then play slow C–G–C changes for 5 minutes at 40 bpm
Switch the all-downstroke pattern to down-up eighth notes (1-and-2-and) over Em–Am at 50 bpm, 4 clean laps in a row
One-minute change drill on the hardest pair (likely C–G): count clean changes, then beat that count on a second run
Learn the D-DU-UDU strumming pattern and loop it over G–C at 55 bpm until you get 4 clean laps without stopping
Pick your first song (e.g. Knockin' on Heaven's Door: G–D–Am–C) and play just its chord progression on downstrokes at 60 bpm, 3 passes
Play that song's verse section end to end with the strumming pattern, 3 run-throughs without stopping, and write down the one spot that breaks
Isolate the spot that broke last time: loop just that bar/change 10 times slowly, then play the verse 3 times clean and log whether the break moves
Learn the chorus of song 1 and play verse straight into chorus without stopping, 3 passes at 60 bpm
Add a second song with an easy progression (e.g. Three Little Birds: A–D–E) and play 3 passes of its progression with the D-DU-UDU pattern at 60 bpm
Close out song 2: learn its chorus, then play verse straight into chorus 3 times without stopping, and finish by running both songs back to back once as a mini set
Record one full song start to finish on your phone, listen back once, and write down the 3 spots that sound weakest
Dynamic contrast pass: verse with light downstrokes, chorus with full D-DU-UDU at 65 bpm, 3 passes per song so the chorus is audibly louder
Record song 1 again with the verse-light/chorus-loud plan at 65 bpm, A/B it against your earlier take, and write down whether the chorus is now clearly louder
Stand up and play both songs back to back as one mini set with no stops, recorded in a single take; note the total time and the two spots where you flinched
Pick the single song for your demo and play it 3 times in a row with a 30-second pause between takes, holding the same tempo and dynamics each time
